correctness.rationale: All graph and metric quantifiers are fixed. The three sums per edge are explicit. Cross-edge sums have two nonzero edge-label coordinates and cannot collide with within-edge sums; for fixed signs, equal cross-edge sums would require equal signed differences of distinct graph-edge endpoint unit vectors, impossible in a simple graph. Class intersections recover core edges, unshared pairs recover pendant edges, and residual edge count recovers isolated K2 components. The squared-distance signature identity plus affine spanning gives exact midpoint equivalence. Exact arithmetic checker passed 814 exhaustive and 157 seeded cases; infinite validity rests on the stated proof, not testing.

value.rationale: It answers a natural complete inverse question for a standard graph-indexed Euclidean family: can a polytope metric with neither graph labels nor ambient coordinates recover the graph? The answer gives an explicit collision classification and O(m^3) exact algorithm avoiding expensive facet enumeration, handles arbitrary disconnected graphs and sharp isolated-vertex nonidentifiability, and yields a complete congruence classification; this has nontrivial structural and algorithmic content beyond counting individual midpoint relations.
